# Index every link by meaning and return its best passages

## Intent

Keyword search finds a link only when the query shares words with it, so a page saved as "Durable Objects alarms" is lost to a search for "scheduling work in the background on Cloudflare". Alexandria keeps, for every user, a private index of what each of their links means, built from the text it already stores and kept current as that text changes, and returns the passages of the owner's links that best answer a question. It is the foundation that search by meaning and asking the library are built on, and it never lets one user's library inform another's, nor keeps anything of a link once the link is gone.

## Goals

- A link's text is findable by meaning within 60 seconds (p95) of its reader text, title, summary, topic, tags or note being stored or changed, outside a backfill.
- Every link that existed before this feature is findable by meaning once the backfill has run, without the owner doing anything; a library of 10,000 links is fully indexed within 3 hours.
- `GET /api/v1/passages?q=<question>` returns the passages of the owner's links that best match the question by meaning, each with its link's id, title and URL, even when the question shares no word with the link.
- An agent calling the MCP tool `search_passages` receives the same passages.
- A link deleted (by the owner, by decay's removal or by account deletion) is never again returned by a passage request, and its passages and index entries are gone within the 10 minutes account deletion promises.
- No request or background job of one user reads, ranks with or returns another user's text.

## Non-goals

- **Search by meaning** (`GET /api/v1/search?mode=hybrid`, the `match` and `meaning` fields, the website's search on Enter, `search_links` searching by meaning). It is the next package, `11_hybrid_search`, built on this index (Design Decision 19).
- **Asking the library** (`POST /api/v1/ask`, the Ask page, streaming answers from the owner's AI provider). It is the package after that, `12_ask_the_library`, built on passages (Design Decision 19).
- Cloudflare AI Search (formerly AutoRAG), the managed indexing service. Considered and rejected in favour of an index Alexandria writes and deletes itself (Design Decision 1).
- Searching workspaces by meaning, searching across users, or any shared or pooled index of content.
- Embedding images, the raw snapshot HTML, or anything other than the text Alexandria already stores (title, summary, topic, tags, note, reader text).
- Related links (the owner's links nearest in meaning to one link). A later PRD.
- Paying for embeddings with the owner's key. Embeddings run on Workers AI on the deployment's account (Design Decision 4).
- Showing the backfill's progress or a link's index state anywhere (Design Decision 9).
- Changing the query language: the prefix filters and the 200-character cap stay as they are.
- Changing the export: passages and vectors are derived data and are not exported.

## Background

PRD 02 (`docs/prd/02-find-links-by-meaning-and-ask-the-library.md`) lifts PRD 01's non-goal "Semantic / vector search". Its owner chose to build it as three packages (Design Decision 19); this is the first, the index and the passages that the other two use.

What exists today:

- **Keyword search.** `GET /api/v1/search` (`src/worker/search/routes.ts`) parses the query into free words and prefix filters (`parseQuery` in `src/worker/search/query.ts`: `tag:`, `topic:`, `host:`, `in:`, `is:`, `state:`; 200 characters at most; `query_too_long` and `invalid_filter`), turns the filters into SQL conditions on the links (`filterConditions`, which also leaves archived links out unless a `state:` filter is given), and ranks matches from an FTS5 index (`link_search`, migration `0006_search_index.sql`) that triggers keep current on every change of a link's title, summary, topic, tags, note or reader text. `parseLimit` in `src/worker/api/pagination.ts` reads a page size.
- **Stored text.** The fetch consumer (`src/worker/fetcher/queue.ts`) stores a page's or PDF's reader text, at most 500,000 characters, in `link_texts`; enrichment (`storeEnrichment` in `src/worker/enrich/queue.ts`) stores summary, topic and tags; the owner edits title, summary, tags and topic (`applyEdit` in `src/worker/enrich/edits.ts`) and the note (`setLinkNote` in `src/worker/links/store.ts`, at most 20,000 characters) through `PATCH /api/v1/links/{id}`; topics and tags are renamed and merged by `renameEntry` and `mergeEntry` in `src/worker/search/vocabulary.ts`.
- **Queues and crons.** One Worker (`src/worker/index.ts`) consumes `alexandria-fetch`, `alexandria-enrich`, `alexandria-liveness` and `alexandria-account`, and runs three Cron Triggers: hourly (decay and liveness), every minute (the import dispatcher, `src/worker/imports/dispatch.ts`) and every 5 minutes (the account deletion sweep). `accountActive` (`src/worker/account/deletion.ts`) stops background work for an account marked for deletion.
- **Deletion paths.** A link is deleted by the owner (`deleteLink` in `src/worker/links/store.ts`, `DELETE /api/v1/links/{id}`), by decay's removal (`removalStatements` in `src/worker/decay/decay.ts`) and by account deletion (`runDeletion` in `src/worker/account/deletion.ts`), whose job finds the account's tables from the schema (every table with a `link_id` or `user_id` column, except tables a trigger inserts into) and removes everything of the account within 10 minutes.
- **The MCP server** (`src/worker/mcp/`). Nine tools, each a request to the Worker's own API as the token's user; `outcomeOf` in `tools.ts` turns a 2xx into structured content, a 4xx error envelope into a tool error, and anything else into `internal_error`. `INSTRUCTIONS` in `server.ts` is the text an agent receives on initialize.
- **Platform.** `wrangler.jsonc` binds D1, R2, the queues, a Durable Object and the crons; `scripts/provision.sh` creates the resources before a deploy. D1 cannot load a vector extension. Every API response the Worker tests receive is compared with the OpenAPI document (`src/worker/api/openapi.ts`).

Constraints:

- Constraint: Cloudflare **Vectorize** holds the vectors and **Workers AI** computes the embeddings (owner's choice). Both are new bindings and new resources `scripts/provision.sh` creates.
- Constraint: the unit and integration tests (`make test`, Vitest in workerd) and the end-to-end tests (`make e2e`, Playwright against `wrangler dev`) run without a Cloudflare account, as they do today; neither Vectorize nor Workers AI is reachable there.
- Constraint: strict per-user separation (PRD 01); the MCP server reaches the library only through the API, as today.

## Requirements

### Indexing by meaning

- When a link's reader text is stored (first fetch, refresh), or its title, summary, topic, tags or note change (enrichment, the owner's edit, a rename or merge of a topic or tag), the link is queued for indexing. Within 60 seconds (p95) a passage request reflects its new text.
- What is indexed for a link: its title, summary, topic, tags and note, together, and the first 50,000 characters of its reader text, cut into passages of at most 1,500 characters. Text past 50,000 characters of reader text is in no passage. A link with no reader text (pending, unreachable, not a web page, a PDF without text) is indexed on its title, summary, topic, tags and note alone.
- Links in every state are indexed, archived links included; which states a request returns is decided by its filters.
- When a link's text changes, nothing of its previous text is returned once the new text is indexed.
- Failure: Workers AI or Vectorize is unavailable or refuses a request. The link stays findable by keyword; its indexing is retried up to 5 times; after the last retry it is left as it was (unindexed, or indexed on its previous text) and the backfill picks it up. Nothing is shown on the link and nothing else about it changes.
- Failure: a link's text changes again while its indexing is in flight. The older job stores nothing; the job queued for the newer text indexes it.
- Failure: a link is deleted while its indexing is in flight. Nothing of it remains in the index once the in-flight job ends.
- An account marked for deletion is indexed no more: its jobs write nothing and call neither Workers AI nor Vectorize.

### Backfill

- Every link that has no passages, or whose passages were made from older text than its current text, is indexed by a background backfill, without any action of the owner, at most 60 links per minute per user. Users are independent: one user's backfill does not slow another's. A link queued in the last 10 minutes is not queued again.
- The backfill is not shown anywhere: no count, banner, field or state on the link. Until a link is indexed, a passage request does not return it.
- An account marked for deletion is not backfilled.

### Passages

- `GET /api/v1/passages?q=<question>&limit=<n>` returns the passages of the owner's links that best match the question by meaning, best first: `200 {"items": [{"link_id", "title", "url", "passage", "score"}], "meaning": "used"}`. `q` takes the search query language: free words form the question, the prefix filters apply as in search, archived links are left out without `state:`. `limit` is 1 to 20, default 8. A passage is at most 1,500 characters of the link's indexed text. `url` is the link's original URL. `score` is the passage's similarity to the question. Passages below the similarity threshold are not returned, so a question unrelated to anything in the library answers with no items. It records no use.
- At most 3 passages of one link are returned; the rest of the limit goes to other links.
- Refusals: `q` without a free word (absent, empty, blank or filters only): `400 {"error": "invalid_question", "field": "q", "message": "ask with at least one word"}`; a `q` over 200 characters: `query_too_long`, and a refused filter value: `invalid_filter`, as in search; a `limit` that is not an integer from 1 to 20: `400 {"error": "invalid_limit", "field": "limit", "message": "limit must be an integer from 1 to 20"}`.
- Failure: Workers AI or Vectorize fails or has not answered within 5 seconds: `503 {"error": "search_unavailable", "message": "search by meaning is unavailable, try again"}`.
- The MCP tool `search_passages(query, limit?)` is this request, with the same shapes and errors as structured tool results, `search_unavailable` included. The MCP server's instructions text tells an agent to use `search_passages` to answer a question from the library and `get_link_content` to read a whole link.

### Deletion and isolation

- Deleting a link (by the owner, or by decay's removal) removes its passages at once and its index entries within the next minute. Until the index has caught up, no passage request returns it: results are checked against the owner's existing passages before they are returned.
- Account deletion removes every index entry and every passage of the account within its 10 minutes.
- When removing index entries fails, they are removed at a later run; nothing else waits for it.
- The export (`GET /api/v1/export`) is unchanged: vectors and passages are derived data, rebuilt from the links, and not exported.
- No passage request or background job reads or writes index entries of any user other than the one it runs for.

### End-to-end flows

1. The owner adds `https://example.com/durable-object-alarms`; the fetch worker stores the article's reader text; the index worker indexes it; a minute later `GET /api/v1/passages?q=run a task later on cloudflare` returns a passage of the article with its id, title and URL.
2. An agent with a personal access token calls `search_passages("how do I schedule background work on Cloudflare?")` through the MCP server and receives passages of the Durable Objects article with its id, title and URL; no use is recorded.
3. The owner deletes the article; an immediate passage request for its subject no longer lists it; at the next every-minute run its index entries are removed.
4. Links stored before the index existed (no passages) are indexed by the every-minute backfill without any action of the owner, and a passage request then returns them.
5. The owner deletes the account; the deletion job removes its passages, and once it is done and the next every-minute run has passed, the index holds no entry of the account.

## Design Decisions

1. **Build the index in Alexandria with Vectorize and Workers AI, not Cloudflare AI Search.** Owner's choice. AI Search indexes an R2 bucket on a sync schedule, which holds raw HTML rather than the stored reader text, summary and note; separates users by path filters rather than by the authenticated user; and delays deletion past the account deletion promise.
4. **Embeddings run on Workers AI on the deployment's Cloudflare account, paid by the operator.** Owner's decision. It amends PRD 01 DD9 for embeddings only: Anthropic offers no embeddings API, so the owner's key cannot cover them. Every text sent for embedding is the owner's own stored text, sent to Cloudflare, where it is already stored.
6. **Agents get passages (`search_passages`), not an ask tool.** Owner's decision. An agent has its own model; Alexandria supplies the retrieval and spends nothing of the owner's key on an agent's behalf.
9. **Backfill at 60 links a minute per user, shown nowhere.** Owner's decision. 10,000 links index in about 3 hours.
11. **Reader text indexed up to 50,000 characters.** Owner's decision: almost every article whole, long PDFs bounded.
13. **The similarity threshold is one fixed constant**, the same for passages, search by meaning and asking. Its provisional value is in Design Decision 21.
14. **Passages of at most 1,500 characters, at most 3 per link.** Enough context for an answer from several sources within the 20,000 characters enrichment already sends a provider.
19. **Three packages, not two.** Owner's choice in this run: `10_meaning_index` (this one: indexing, backfill, deletion and isolation, passages and `search_passages`), then `11_hybrid_search` (`mode=hybrid`, ranking, the fallback, the website's search on Enter, `search_links`), then `12_ask_the_library`. Each later package is written by its own run.
20. **The embedding model is `@cf/baai/bge-m3`, in a Vectorize index `alexandria-passages` of 1,024 dimensions with the cosine metric.** Links come in any language (`links.language`), and bge-m3 is multilingual with an input window that holds a 1,500-character passage whole. `scripts/provision.sh` creates the index when it does not exist.
21. **The similarity threshold is 0.5 (cosine), provisional**, recorded in a new ADR with the model choice. No library is reachable to tune it against in this run; changing the constant later changes no other behaviour.
22. **One Vectorize namespace per user, named by the user id, and every result checked against the user's passages in D1.** Two independent locks: a query reads only its user's namespace, and a vector whose passage is not the requesting user's current passage is dropped.
23. **Passages are kept in D1 beside the links, each with the id of its vector, `{link_id}:{version}:{n}`.** They can then be returned, filtered and deleted with the links; a new text version gets new vector ids, so a vector of older text matches no current passage and is never returned.
24. **A text version per link, kept by triggers** as `link_search` is kept, moves with every change of the indexed fields (title, summary, topic, tags, note, reader text, a rename of its topic or tags). A link whose passages carry an older version, or that has none, is stale.
25. **Vector deletions go through a queue in D1**: a table that a trigger fills with the vector id of every passage deleted, drained by the every-minute run. Every deletion path (the owner, decay, account deletion, re-indexing) then removes vectors the same way, a failed Vectorize call is retried at the next run, and the account deletion job, which leaves trigger-kept tables alone, cannot remove the queue before it is drained.
26. **A new queue `alexandria-index` (`INDEX_QUEUE`, batch size 10, 5 retries) carries one message `{user_id, link_id}` per link to index.** The writes queue a link only when its text version moved past its passages' version.
27. **The backfill runs in the existing every-minute Cron Trigger**, beside the import dispatcher and the vector-deletion drain.
28. **A passage request takes the 100 nearest passages from Vectorize, then applies the threshold, the user check and the filters in D1.** A filtered question whose matches lie outside the 100 nearest returns fewer passages; accepted for a personal library.
29. **The question embedded is the query's free words, joined by single spaces**; the filters are not embedded.
30. **Passages are cut in order**: first the link's title, summary, topic, tags and note joined by line breaks (more than one passage when the note is long), then the first 50,000 characters of the reader text, each cut at the last paragraph break, else sentence end, else space, before 1,500 characters.
31. **The fakes.** The Worker tests install fake `AI` and `VECTORIZE` bindings on `env`; `wrangler dev` cannot take such fakes, so the end-to-end tests set `MEANING_FAKE_URL` to a local fake service (`e2e/fake-meaning.ts`), as `ORIGIN_PROXY_URL` points the fetcher at `e2e/fake-origin.ts`. Both fakes embed by one fixed table of word groups, so that words of one group ("later", "alarm", "schedule", "background") are near in meaning and unrelated text scores below the threshold. Miniflare starts a Worker that binds `ai` and `vectorize` without an account and fails only when they are called (verified in Miniflare's source), so the bindings can be declared in `wrangler.jsonc` for every environment.
32. **The backfill takes a user's stale links most recently used first**, so the links the owner reaches for become findable first.
33. **A write whose index message cannot be sent still succeeds**: the failure is logged, and the backfill picks the link up, since its passages stay older than its text.

## Verified External API

Read from the installed `@cloudflare/workers-types` 5.20261107.1 (`index.d.ts`), the version the repository's lockfile holds (`^5.20261107.1`):

- `Vectorize.query(vector: VectorFloatArray | number[], options?: VectorizeQueryOptions): Promise<VectorizeMatches>`, with `VectorizeQueryOptions { topK?: number; namespace?: string; returnValues?: boolean; returnMetadata?: boolean | VectorizeMetadataRetrievalLevel; filter?: VectorizeVectorMetadataFilter }` and `VectorizeMatches { matches: VectorizeMatch[]; count: number }`; `VectorizeMatch` is the vector's `id`, `namespace` and `metadata` with `score: number`.
- `Vectorize.upsert(vectors: VectorizeVector[]): Promise<VectorizeAsyncMutation>`, `deleteByIds(ids: string[]): Promise<VectorizeAsyncMutation>`; `VectorizeVector { id: string; values: VectorFloatArray | number[]; namespace?: string; metadata?: Record<string, VectorizeVectorMetadata> }`; mutations are asynchronous (`VectorizeAsyncMutation { mutationId: string }`).
- `Ai.run(model, inputs, options?)`; `@cf/baai/bge-m3` takes `{ text: string | string[]; truncate_inputs?: boolean }` and its output is a union, of which the embedding form is `{ shape?: number[]; data?: number[][]; pooling?: "mean" | "cls" }`.
- `wrangler vectorize create <name> --dimensions <n> --metric cosine` and `wrangler vectorize get <name>` exist in the installed wrangler 4.158.0 (`wrangler vectorize --help`).
- Miniflare 5.20261101.0-beta (`dist/src/index.js`): an `ai` or `vectorize` binding without `remote: true` is created with a warning and no remote connection; its calls fail.
- **Unverified** (not in the typings): bge-m3's vector dimensions (1,024 assumed) and input limit; Vectorize's limits (namespaces per index, the `topK` maximum with `returnMetadata: "none"` (100 assumed), ids per `upsert` and `deleteByIds` call (1,000 assumed), id length (64 bytes assumed)); Workers AI's texts per call (100 assumed); both services' prices.

## Glossary

- **embedding**: a vector of numbers computed from a piece of text, such that texts of similar meaning have nearby vectors.
- **passage**: a contiguous piece of a link's indexed text, at most 1,500 characters, the unit the index matches and returns.
- **similarity threshold**: the fixed similarity a passage must reach to be returned.
- **text version**: a counter per link that moves with every change of its indexed text; passages carry the version they were made from.
- **stale**: a link with no passages, or whose passages carry an older text version than the link's.
- **backfill**: the background indexing of stale links.
- **index worker**: the consumer of `alexandria-index`, which indexes one link per message.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Queue a link for indexing when its indexed text changes

**Rationale:** An index that lags behind the owner's edits answers with text the link no longer has.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN the fetch worker stores a link's reader text, on its first fetch or on a refresh, THE Worker SHALL send one index message {user_id, link_id} for the link on INDEX_QUEUE after the text is stored
   → exactly one message {user_id, link_id} on INDEX_QUEUE for the link per write that moved its text version
   Check: integration
   - setup: INDEX_QUEUE replaced by a recorder (a new recordIndexQueue() in src/worker/test/helpers.ts, beside recordFetchQueue)
   - setup: a signed-in user with an AI key the fake provider accepts
   ```
   in a new src/worker/meaning/indexing.test.ts, one table over the writes, each row: sent = recordIndexQueue(); perform(write); assert sent.filter(m => m.body.link_id == id).length == expected. Rows: deliverFetches of a first fetch that stores reader text -> 1; deliverFetches of a refresh -> 1; deliverEnrichments storing summary, topic and tags -> 1; PATCH /api/v1/links/{id} with a new title, a new summary, new tags, a new topic, a new note -> 1 each; PATCH /api/v1/tags/{id} renaming a tag carried by 3 links -> 1 for each of the 3; POST /api/v1/topics/{id}/merge of a topic carried by 2 links -> 1 for each of the 2; PATCH with the title the link already has -> 0; POST /api/v1/links/{id}/pin -> 0; POST /api/v1/links/{id}/archive -> 0; GET /api/v1/links/{id}/open -> 0
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHEN enrichment stores a link's summary, topic or tags, THE Worker SHALL send one index message {user_id, link_id} for the link on INDEX_QUEUE after they are stored
   → exactly one message {user_id, link_id} on INDEX_QUEUE for the link
   Check: same as REQ-1.1
1. [REQ-1.3] WHEN the owner's PATCH /api/v1/links/{id} changes the link's title, summary, tags, topic or note, THE Worker SHALL send one index message {user_id, link_id} for the link on INDEX_QUEUE after the edit is stored
   → exactly one message {user_id, link_id} on INDEX_QUEUE for the link; the PATCH answers as it does today
   Check: same as REQ-1.1
1. [REQ-1.4] WHEN the owner renames or merges a topic or tag, THE Worker SHALL send one index message {user_id, link_id} on INDEX_QUEUE for every link whose text the change altered: each link carrying the renamed topic or tag, or each link the merge moved onto the survivor, in batches of at most 100 messages
   → one message per carrying link; the rename or merge answers as it does today
   Check: same as REQ-1.1
1. [REQ-1.5] IF a write leaves a link's title, summary, topic, tags, note and reader text as they were (a pin, an archive, a use, a PATCH that sets the values the link already has), THEN THE Worker SHALL send no index message for the link
   → no message on INDEX_QUEUE for the link
   Check: same as REQ-1.1
1. [REQ-1.6] THE Worker SHALL make a link's new text returnable by a passage request within 60 seconds (p95) of the write that queued it, outside a backfill
   Check: same as PATH-1

### REQ-2: Cut a link's text into passages and index them

**Rationale:** The passage is the unit the index matches and returns, so what goes into passages is what can be found.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN the index worker receives a message for a link of an account not marked for deletion, THE index worker SHALL cut the link's title, summary, topic, tags and note, then the first 50,000 characters of its reader text, into passages of at most 1,500 characters, embed them with @cf/baai/bge-m3, upsert one vector per passage into the namespace named by the user's id, and store the passages in D1 with the text version they were made from
   → the message is acknowledged; the link's passages in D1 are, in order, its title, summary, topic, tags and note, then its reader text, each at most 1,500 characters and marked with the link's current text version; the index holds one vector per passage, id {link_id}:{version}:{n}, in namespace user_id
   Check: integration
   - setup: fake AI and VECTORIZE bindings installed on env by a new src/worker/test/meaning.ts (a deterministic embedder over fixed word groups, an in-memory index with namespaces, and switches to fail or stall each call)
   - setup: a new deliverIndexing(bodies, bindings) in src/worker/test/helpers.ts, beside deliverFetches
   ```
   in src/worker/meaning/indexing.test.ts, a table over links, each row: r = deliverIndexing([{user_id, link_id}]); assert r.acked == ['m0']; rows = passages of the link in position order; assert rows[0] starts with the title and holds the summary, topic, tags and note; assert every row is at most 1,500 characters and carries the link's text version; assert the fake index holds exactly one vector per row, id `${link_id}:${version}:${n}`, namespace user.id. Rows: an active page with 4,000 characters of reader text and a note -> metadata passage, then reader passages; a pending link with no reader text -> metadata passages only; an unreachable link, a link noted 'not a web page' and a PDF without text -> metadata passages only; an archived link -> indexed like an active one; a link with a 20,000-character note -> the note spread over several metadata passages
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] THE index worker SHALL for any reader text, put no character past its first 50,000 characters into a passage, and cut the rest so that every passage is non-empty, at most 1,500 characters, and the passages in order give back the first 50,000 characters apart from the whitespace at the cuts
   Check: property
   ```
   in a new src/worker/meaning/cut.test.ts, with fast-check over reader texts of 0 to 500,000 characters built from words, sentences and paragraph breaks (and the boundary lengths 1,499, 1,500, 1,501, 50,000 and 50,001 as explicit examples): ps = cutPassages({title, summary, topic, tags, note: ''}, text).slice(metadataCount); assert ps.every(p => p.length >= 1 && p.length <= 1500); assert normalise(ps.join(' ')) == normalise(text.slice(0, 50000)); a text of 50,001 characters whose last character is a unique marker never shows the marker
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] WHERE a link has no reader text (pending, unreachable, not a web page, a PDF without text), THE index worker SHALL index the link on its title, summary, topic, tags and note alone
   Check: same as REQ-2.1
1. [REQ-2.4] THE index worker SHALL index the links of every state, archived links included
   Check: same as REQ-2.1
1. [REQ-2.5] WHEN a link that already has passages is indexed again from changed text, THE index worker SHALL replace its passages with the new ones in one D1 write and queue the vector ids of its previous passages for deletion
   → the link's passages in D1 are only those of the new text version, none holding the previous text; every previous vector id is in the vector deletion queue
   Check: integration
   ```
   in src/worker/meaning/indexing.test.ts: index a link whose note reads about alarms; PATCH its note to text about gardening; deliverIndexing again; assert every passage of the link carries the new version and none holds 'alarms'; assert every previous vector id is in the vector deletion queue and the fake index received the new ids in namespace user.id
   ```

### REQ-3: Leave a link as it was when its indexing cannot finish

**Rationale:** A failed or overtaken index job must never leave half of a link's text, older text, or text of a deleted link behind.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] IF Workers AI or Vectorize throws or refuses a call while a link is indexed, THEN THE index worker SHALL hand the message back for retry and leave the link's passages, row and API view as they were
   → the message is retried, not acknowledged; the link's passages in D1 and the body of GET /api/v1/links/{id}, updated_at included, are unchanged
   Check: integration
   ```
   in src/worker/meaning/indexing.test.ts, a table over the failing call {embedding throws, upsert throws}, for a link never indexed and a link indexed on earlier text: before = (passages of the link, GET /api/v1/links/{id}.json); fake.fail(call); r = deliverIndexing([...]); assert r.retried == ['m0'] and r.acked == []; assert (passages, link view) == before
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] IF the link's text version moves past the version the job read before the job stores its passages, THEN THE index worker SHALL store nothing and queue every vector id the job upserted for deletion
   → the message is acknowledged; the link's passages in D1 are unchanged; every id the job upserted is in the vector deletion queue
   Check: integration
   ```
   in src/worker/meaning/indexing.test.ts, a table over what happens while the fake embedder runs (its onEmbed hook): {PATCH the link's note, DELETE /api/v1/links/{id}}: r = deliverIndexing([...]); assert r.acked == ['m0']; assert the link's passages are what they were before (none for the deleted link); assert every id the fake index received from this job is in the vector deletion queue
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] IF the link is deleted while its index job is in flight, THEN THE index worker SHALL store nothing and queue every vector id the job upserted for deletion, so that nothing of the link remains in the index once the queue is drained
   → the message is acknowledged; no passage of the link in D1; every id the job upserted is in the vector deletion queue
   Check: same as REQ-3.2
1. [REQ-3.4] IF a message arrives for a link that no longer exists, or of an account marked for deletion, THEN THE index worker SHALL acknowledge the message without calling Workers AI or Vectorize and write nothing
   → the message is acknowledged; the fake AI and VECTORIZE bindings record no call; no passage is written
   Check: integration
   ```
   in src/worker/meaning/indexing.test.ts, a table over {a deleted link id, a link of an account whose deletion_requested_at is set}: r = deliverIndexing([...]); assert r.acked == ['m0']; assert fake.calls == []; assert count('link_passages', 'link_id = ?', id) == 0
   ```

### REQ-4: Backfill stale links in the background

**Rationale:** The library the owner already has must become findable by meaning without the owner doing anything.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN the every-minute Cron Trigger (* * * * *) runs, THE every-minute run SHALL send, for each user whose account is not marked for deletion, index messages for at most 60 of the user's stale links that were not queued in the last 10 minutes, and record when each was queued
   → at most 60 messages on INDEX_QUEUE per user per run; no link queued twice within 10 minutes; a link with no passages and a link whose passages carry an older text version are both stale
   Check: integration
   - setup: INDEX_QUEUE replaced by recordIndexQueue()
   - setup: the clock fixed with setNow
   ```
   in a new src/worker/meaning/backfill.test.ts, running worker.scheduled with cron '* * * * *' as src/worker/imports/imports.test.ts does: user A has 150 links with no passages, user B has 4 links with no passages and 1 indexed link whose note was then changed, user C (deletion_requested_at set) has 5 links with no passages. Run at t: assert A gets 60 distinct messages, B 5, C 0. Run at t+1 min: assert A gets 60 others, none repeated, B 0. Run at t+2 min: A gets the last 30. Run at t+11 min with nothing indexed: A's first 60 are queued again
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] THE every-minute run SHALL keep each user's backfill independent: one user's stale links never reduce the number of links the same run queues for another user
   Check: same as REQ-4.1
1. [REQ-4.3] WHILE an account is marked for deletion, THE every-minute run SHALL queue none of its links for indexing
   Check: same as REQ-4.1
1. [REQ-4.4] THE every-minute run SHALL make every link of a library of 10,000 stale links findable by meaning within 3 hours of the backfill starting
   Check: same as REQ-4.1
1. [REQ-4.5] THE index worker SHALL expose no index or backfill state: indexing a link changes neither its API view nor its place in the stream's change feed
   Check: integration
   ```
   in src/worker/meaning/indexing.test.ts: before = GET /api/v1/links/{id}.json and GET /api/v1/links?since=<server time>; deliverIndexing([...]); assert GET /api/v1/links/{id}.json deep-equals before (updated_at included) and the change feed since that time lists nothing
   ```

### REQ-5: Return the passages that best answer a question

**Rationale:** Passages are what an agent, and later the search and the answers, read from the index.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] WHEN a client sends GET /api/v1/passages with a q holding at least one free word, THE Alexandria API SHALL embed the free words joined by single spaces, take the 100 nearest vectors in the user's namespace, keep those whose score is at least the similarity threshold of 0.5 and whose id is a current passage of one of the user's links, and return them best first, recording no use
   → 200 {items: [{link_id, title, url, passage, score}], meaning: 'used'}, items ordered by score descending, every score at least 0.5, url the link's original URL; no link_uses row and no change of use_count or last_used_at
   Check: integration
   - setup: the fake AI and VECTORIZE bindings of src/worker/test/meaning.ts
   - setup: three links indexed through deliverIndexing: an article about Durable Objects alarms, one about Cloudflare Queues, one about growing tomatoes
   ```
   in a new src/worker/meaning/passages.test.ts, a table over q: 'run a task later' (no word shared with the alarms article) -> first item is the alarms link; 'tomato soil compost' -> first item is the tomatoes link; 'quarterly tax return' -> items == []; each row: r = GET /api/v1/passages?q=...; assert r.status == 200 and r.json.meaning == 'used'; assert scores descending and >= 0.5; assert items[0].url == the link's original_url and items[0].title == its title; assert count('link_uses') and the links' use_count and last_used_at are unchanged
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] THE Alexandria API SHALL return at most limit passages, limit being 1 to 20 and 8 when absent, and at most 3 passages of one link, giving the rest of the limit to other links
   Check: integration
   ```
   in src/worker/meaning/passages.test.ts: one link with 6 passages matching the question and 6 other matching links of one passage each; table over limit {absent -> 8 items, 3 of the large link; 2 -> 2 items; 20 -> 9 items, 3 of the large link and one of each other}; each row asserts items.length and that no link_id appears more than 3 times
   ```
1. [REQ-5.3] THE Alexandria API SHALL apply the prefix filters tag:, topic:, host:, in:, is: and state: to the passages' links as filterConditions applies them to search, leaving archived links out unless a state: filter is given
   Check: integration
   ```
   in src/worker/meaning/passages.test.ts: four matching links, one archived, one tagged 'infra', one pinned and in workspace 'Research', one on host docs.example; table over q suffix {'' -> the three not archived; 'state:archived' -> the archived one; 'state:any' -> all four; 'tag:infra' -> the tagged one; 'in:Research' and 'is:pinned' -> the pinned one; 'host:docs.example' -> that one}; each row asserts the set of link_ids
   ```
1. [REQ-5.4] IF q has no free word (absent, empty, blank or filters only), THEN THE Alexandria API SHALL refuse the request without embedding anything
   → 400 {error: 'invalid_question', field: 'q', message: 'ask with at least one word'}; the fake AI binding records no call
   Check: integration
   ```
   in src/worker/meaning/passages.test.ts, one table over (query string -> status, error, field, message): no q, q='', q='   ', q='tag:infra' -> 400 invalid_question, 'q', 'ask with at least one word'; q of 201 characters -> 400 query_too_long, 'q', 'a query of at most 200 characters'; q='alarms state:bogus' -> 400 invalid_filter, 'q', parseQuery's message; limit=0, limit=21, limit=x -> 400 invalid_limit, 'limit', 'limit must be an integer from 1 to 20'; each row asserts the body exactly and that the fake AI binding recorded no call
   ```
1. [REQ-5.5] IF q is over 200 characters or holds a filter value search refuses, THEN THE Alexandria API SHALL refuse the request as GET /api/v1/search refuses it, without embedding anything
   → 400 query_too_long or invalid_filter with field 'q' and parseQuery's message; the fake AI binding records no call
   Check: same as REQ-5.4
1. [REQ-5.6] IF limit is not an integer from 1 to 20, THEN THE Alexandria API SHALL refuse the request without embedding anything
   → 400 {error: 'invalid_limit', field: 'limit', message: 'limit must be an integer from 1 to 20'}
   Check: same as REQ-5.4
1. [REQ-5.7] IF Workers AI or Vectorize fails, or the embedding and the query together have not answered within 5 seconds, THEN THE Alexandria API SHALL answer that search by meaning is unavailable
   → 503 {error: 'search_unavailable', message: 'search by meaning is unavailable, try again'}, answered within 7 seconds of the request; never a 500
   Check: integration

   ```

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-6.1] WHEN an agent calls the tool search_passages with a query and an optional limit, THE MCP server SHALL send GET /api/v1/passages with the query as q and the limit (8 when absent) as the agent's user, and return the API's body

   ```
1. [REQ-6.2] IF the API refuses the passage request (invalid_question, query_too_long, invalid_filter) or answers 503 search_unavailable, THEN THE MCP server SHALL return a tool error that carries the API's error envelope
   → isError true and structuredContent deep-equals the API's {error, field?, message}; search_unavailable is never turned into internal_error
   Check: integration

   in src/worker/mcp/mcp.test.ts under 'search_passages', a table over {query 'tag:infra' -> invalid_question; a query of 201 characters -> query_too_long; 'x state:bogus' -> invalid_filter; the fake embedder failing -> search_unavailable}: r = mcpTool(secret, 'search_passages', {query}); assert r.isError; assert r.structuredContent deep-equals the body of the same GET /api/v1/passages
   ```
1. [REQ-6.3] THE MCP server SHALL list search_passages among its tools, with query a required non-empty string and limit an optional integer from 1 to 20, refusing a limit outside it as invalid_arguments
   Check: integration
   ```
   in src/worker/mcp/mcp.test.ts, extend 'lists exactly the nine tools with their arguments' to the ten tools: assert byName.search_passages.required == ['query'] and properties.limit is an integer with maximum 20; add a row to the existing argument-refusal tests: mcpTool(secret, 'search_passages', {query: 'x', limit: 21}) -> isError with {error: 'invalid_arguments', field: 'limit'}
   ```
1. [REQ-6.4] THE MCP server SHALL tell an agent, in the instructions it receives on initialize, to use search_passages to answer a question from the library and get_link_content to read a whole link
   Check: integration

   in src/worker/mcp/mcp.test.ts, extend 'initializes as the token’s user with its instructions': assert instructions mention search_passages for answering a question and get_link_content for reading a whole link, and still name search_links before add_link
   ```

### REQ-7: Remove a deleted link's passages and index entries

**Rationale:** A link the owner deleted, or decay removed, must stop informing anything at once and leave nothing behind.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-7.1] WHEN the owner deletes a link, or decay's removal deletes it, THE Worker SHALL delete the link's passages in the same D1 write that deletes the link, and queue the vector id of every one of them for deletion
   → no passage of the link in D1 once DELETE /api/v1/links/{id} has answered 204 or the decay run has ended; every vector id of the link is in the vector deletion queue
   Check: integration
   ```
   in a new src/worker/meaning/deletion.test.ts, a table over the deletion path {DELETE /api/v1/links/{id} as the owner, the hourly run removing a link archived remove_days ago (as 'removal by decay' in src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts sets it up)}: index the link with deliverIndexing; ids = its vector ids; perform the deletion; assert count('link_passages', 'link_id = ?', id) == 0; assert every id is in the vector deletion queue
   ```
1. [REQ-7.2] WHEN the every-minute run finds vector ids in the vector deletion queue, THE Worker SHALL delete them from the index with deleteByIds, at most 1,000 ids per call, until the queue is empty, removing each id from the queue once its call has succeeded
   → after the run the fake index holds none of the queued ids and the queue is empty
   Check: integration
   ```
   in src/worker/meaning/deletion.test.ts: insert 2,500 rows into the vector deletion queue and the matching vectors into the fake index; run worker.scheduled with cron '* * * * *'; assert the fake recorded deleteByIds calls of at most 1,000 ids each, covering all 2,500; assert the queue is empty and the fake index holds none of them
   ```
1. [REQ-7.3] IF deleting vector ids from the index fails, THEN THE Worker SHALL keep those ids queued for the next run and carry on with the run's backfill
   → the ids whose call failed are still in the queue after the run; the backfill's index messages of the same run are sent
   Check: integration
   ```
   in src/worker/meaning/deletion.test.ts: queue ids and leave a stale link; fake.fail('deleteByIds'); sent = recordIndexQueue(); run the every-minute cron; assert the ids are still queued and sent holds the stale link; fake.recover(); run again; assert the queue is empty
   ```
1. [REQ-7.4] THE Worker SHALL return no passage of a link that no longer exists, even while its vectors are still in the index
   Check: integration
   ```
   in src/worker/meaning/deletion.test.ts: index the alarms article; DELETE /api/v1/links/{id}; without running the every-minute cron (its vectors still in the fake index), r = GET /api/v1/passages?q=run+a+task+later; assert no item has the link's id
   ```
1. [REQ-7.5] WHEN the account deletion job removes an account, THE Worker SHALL delete every passage of the account with its other rows and queue their vector ids, so that once the job is done and the next every-minute run has passed, the index holds no vector of the account, within the 10 minutes account deletion promises
   → after runDeletion returns 'done' and one every-minute run: no link_passages row of the user, no vector in the user's namespace in the fake index, and an empty vector deletion queue
   Check: integration
   ```
   in src/worker/account/deletion.test.ts under 'the deletion job': index three links of the account with deliverIndexing; mark the account and run the job until 'done' (as the existing tests do); run worker.scheduled with cron '* * * * *'; assert count('link_passages', 'user_id = ?', user.id) == 0, the fake index's namespace user.id is empty and the vector deletion queue is empty; extend the existing check that nothing of the account remains so that it covers the new tables
   ```

**Rationale:** One user's library must never inform, rank with or appear in another's.

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: The owner adds an article and its passage is found by meaning a minute later

1. **owner** adds https://example.com/durable-object-alarms with POST /api/v1/links/batch
2. **Alexandria API** stores the link and queues its fetch
3. **fetch worker** fetches the article, stores its reader text and queues the link on INDEX_QUEUE
4. **index worker** cuts the link's text into passages, embeds them, upserts their vectors in the owner's namespace and stores the passages in D1
5. **owner** requests GET /api/v1/passages?q=run a task later on cloudflare
6. **Alexandria API** returns a passage of the article with its link id, title and original URL

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the built Worker under wrangler dev, local D1, the fetch and index queues and their consumers, the passages route

**Setup:**

- wrangler dev runs with MEANING_FAKE_URL pointing at e2e/fake-meaning.ts, which stands in for Workers AI and Vectorize, and ORIGIN_PROXY_URL at e2e/fake-origin.ts, which serves the article

**End state:**

- within 60 seconds of the add, GET /api/v1/passages returns as its first item a passage of the article, with the new link's id, its title and https://example.com/durable-object-alarms as url

**Pseudocode:**

```
in a new e2e/passages.spec.ts: signIn(page); [id] = addLinkIds(page, [ALARMS]); poll for up to 60 s: r = page.request.get('/api/v1/passages?q=' + encodeURIComponent('run a task later on cloudflare')); until r.items[0]?.link_id == id; assert r.items[0].url == ALARMS
```

### PATH-2: An agent receives passages through search_passages

1. **agent** calls search_passages("how do I schedule background work on Cloudflare?") through /mcp with a personal access token
2. **MCP server** sends GET /api/v1/passages with the query as the token's user
3. **Alexandria API** returns the passages of the Durable Objects article
4. **MCP server** returns them as the tool's structured content

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the MCP server, the passages route, the built Worker under wrangler dev, local D1

**Setup:**

- the article of PATH-1 is indexed
- a personal access token created on the settings page

**End state:**

- the tool result is not an error and its items carry the article's link id, title and URL
- the article's use_count is unchanged

**Pseudocode:**

```
in e2e/mcp.spec.ts, a new test beside 'searches the library and reads a link’s stored text': client = agent(page, secret); r = call(client, 'search_passages', {query: 'how do I schedule background work on Cloudflare?'}); assert !r.isError and r.structuredContent.items[0] has the article's link_id, title and url; assert d1('SELECT use_count ...') is unchanged
```

### PATH-3: The owner deletes a link and it leaves the index

1. **owner** deletes the article with DELETE /api/v1/links/{id}
2. **Alexandria API** deletes the link with its passages and queues their vector ids for deletion
3. **owner** requests passages for its subject and receives none of the article
4. **scheduler** the every-minute run deletes the queued vector ids from the index

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the built Worker under wrangler dev, local D1, the every-minute scheduled handler, the passages route

**Setup:**

- the article of PATH-1 is indexed

**End state:**

- right after the delete, GET /api/v1/passages lists no item of the article
- after the every-minute run, e2e/fake-meaning.ts holds no vector whose id starts with the article's link id

**Pseudocode:**

```
in e2e/passages.spec.ts: page.request.delete('/api/v1/links/' + id); r = page.request.get('/api/v1/passages?q=...'); assert no item has link_id id; page.request.get('/cdn-cgi/local/scheduled?cron=*+*+*+*+*'); assert (await fakeMeaning.vectors()).every(v => !v.id.startsWith(id))
```

### PATH-4: Links stored before the index existed are backfilled

1. **scheduler** the every-minute run queues the owner's links that have no passages
2. **index worker** indexes each queued link
3. **owner** requests GET /api/v1/passages and receives passages of those links

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the every-minute scheduled handler, the index queue and its consumer, the built Worker under wrangler dev, local D1

**Setup:**

- two links of the owner with reader text written straight into local D1 (the d1() helper of e2e/helpers.ts), with no passages

**End state:**

- after the every-minute run, GET /api/v1/passages returns passages of both links within 60 seconds

**Pseudocode:**

```
in e2e/passages.spec.ts: d1(INSERT two links and their link_texts for the signed-in user); page.request.get('/cdn-cgi/local/scheduled?cron=*+*+*+*+*'); poll for up to 60 s until GET /api/v1/passages?q=... lists both link ids
```

### PATH-5: The owner deletes the account and the index holds nothing of it

1. **owner** deletes the account from the settings page
2. **account deletion worker** removes the account's rows, its passages among them, and queues their vector ids for deletion
3. **scheduler** the every-minute run deletes the queued vector ids from the index

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the account deletion job, the every-minute scheduled handler, the built Worker under wrangler dev, local D1

**Setup:**

- the account has links whose passages are indexed

**End state:**

- once the deletion has finished and the every-minute run has passed, local D1 holds no link_passages row of the account and e2e/fake-meaning.ts holds no vector in its namespace

**Pseudocode:**

```
extends 'is deleted from the settings page and nothing of it remains' in e2e/account.spec.ts: before deleting, poll until d1('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM link_passages WHERE user_id = ...') > 0; after the existing wait for the deletion, run '/cdn-cgi/local/scheduled?cron=*+*+*+*+*'; assert the count is 0 and (await fakeMeaning.vectors(userId)).length == 0
```

# Tasks

## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `make test`
- **linter:** `make lint`
- **spec_tests:** `npx vitest run src/worker/meaning src/worker/mcp src/worker/account src/worker/fetcher/fetch.test.ts src/worker/enrich src/worker/search/vocabulary.test.ts src/worker/links/links.test.ts src/worker/decay/decay.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- `02` — its fetch consumer queues indexing after it stores a link's reader text
- `03` — its enrichment and the owner's edits queue indexing after they store summary, topic, tags or title
- `04` — a link's note is indexed, and its edit through PATCH /api/v1/links/{id} queues indexing
- `05` — decay's removal deletes a link's passages and queues its vectors for deletion
- `06` — passages reuse its query parser and filters, and its renames and merges of topics and tags queue indexing
- `08` — adds the tool search_passages to its MCP server and changes its instructions text
- `09` — its account deletion job removes the account's passages, whose vectors are then drained; the export stays as it is

## Tasks

### 1. Lay down the index's schema, bindings, backend, fakes and passage cutting (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-2.2

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the cutting behaviours to a new src/worker/meaning/cut.test.ts (a fast-check property over reader texts of up to 500,000 characters, with the boundary lengths 1,499, 1,500, 1,501, 50,000 and 50,001 as explicit examples) and confirm they fail
- 1.2 Write cutPassages in src/worker/meaning/cut.ts: first the link's title, summary, topic, tags (joined by spaces) and note, joined by line breaks and cut like any text, then the first 50,000 characters of the reader text; each piece is cut at the last paragraph break, else the last sentence end, else the last space, before 1,500 characters, a run of 1,500 characters without a space at 1,500; no passage is empty or blank
- 1.3 Add migrations/0011_meaning_index.sql: link_passages (the vector id as primary key, link_id and user_id referencing links and users ON DELETE CASCADE, the text version, the position, the text); a per-link index state holding the text version, the version its passages were made from and when it was last queued, with ON DELETE CASCADE to its link (the account deletion job leaves tables a trigger inserts into to their triggers); triggers that move the text version on every change of a link's title, summary, topic_id or note, of its link_tags and link_texts rows, and of the name of its topic or tags, as migration 0006 keeps link_search; and vector_deletions (vector_id, user_id), without a foreign key, filled by a trigger after every delete on link_passages. A link without a state row, or without passages, counts as stale, so the links stored before the migration need no rows
- 1.4 Declare in wrangler.jsonc the ai binding AI, the vectorize binding VECTORIZE on the index alexandria-passages, and the queue alexandria-index as producer INDEX_QUEUE and consumer (max_batch_size 10, max_retries 5), none of them with remote: true and none in the previews block; add AI, VECTORIZE, INDEX_QUEUE, the IndexMessage type {user_id, link_id} and the optional MEANING_FAKE_URL to src/worker/env.ts
- 1.5 Write src/worker/meaning/backend.ts: one interface {embed(texts), upsert(namespace, vectors), query(namespace, vector, topK), deleteByIds(ids)} over env.AI.run('@cf/baai/bge-m3', {text}) in calls of at most 100 texts (an answer without the data array is a failure) and env.VECTORIZE (query with returnValues false and returnMetadata 'none'; at most 1,000 vectors or ids per call); when MEANING_FAKE_URL is set, the same interface over HTTP to that URL instead, for the end-to-end tests only; and the exported similarity threshold 0.5
- 1.6 Add src/worker/test/meaning.ts: fake AI and VECTORIZE bindings with a deterministic embedder over a fixed table of word groups (for example later, alarm, schedule, background, cron; cloudflare, worker, durable, queue; tomato, soil, garden, compost), normalised so that texts sharing a group score at least 0.5 and unrelated texts below it, an in-memory index keyed by namespace, a record of every call, fail, stall and recover switches per call, an onEmbed hook and a switch that makes queries ignore namespaces; install them on env before every Worker test from src/worker/test/setup.ts
- 1.7 Add e2e/fake-meaning.ts, a local HTTP service answering the backend's HTTP form with the same embedder (one module both fakes import) and an in-memory index, with a /__vectors listing for the end-to-end assertions; start it in playwright.config.ts and pass --var MEANING_FAKE_URL to wrangler dev
- 1.8 Document the AI, VECTORIZE and INDEX_QUEUE bindings and MEANING_FAKE_URL in docs/configuration.md

### 2. Index one link per message from INDEX_QUEUE (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-2.1, REQ-2.3, REQ-2.4, REQ-2.5, REQ-3, REQ-4.5, REQ-8.2

**Depends on:** 1

**Steps:**

- 2.1 Add the indexing behaviours to a new src/worker/meaning/indexing.test.ts, with deliverIndexing(bodies, bindings) added to src/worker/test/helpers.ts beside deliverFetches, and confirm they fail
- 2.2 Route batches of alexandria-index in the queue handler of src/worker/index.ts to a new handleIndexBatch in src/worker/meaning/indexing.ts
- 2.3 For each message, acknowledge it without calling Workers AI or Vectorize when the account is not active (accountActive), when the link no longer exists, or when its passages already carry its current text version
- 2.4 Otherwise read the link's title, summary, topic, tags and note from link_views, the first 50,000 characters of its link_texts row and its current text version, and cut them with cutPassages
- 2.5 Embed the passages and upsert one vector per passage into the namespace named by the user's id, with ids {link_id}:{version}:{n}
- 2.6 Store the result in one D1 batch whose writes all depend on the link still existing with the text version the job read: delete its previous passages (the trigger queues their vector ids), insert the new ones, record the version its passages now carry
- 2.7 When that condition no longer holds (the text moved on, or the link was deleted), insert every vector id the job upserted into vector_deletions, store nothing else and acknowledge the message
- 2.8 When Workers AI or Vectorize throws, hand the message back with retry() and write nothing; in no case touch the links row, so updated_at and the stream's change feed stay as they were

**Touches:**

- `src/worker/meaning/indexing.ts`
- `src/worker/meaning/indexing.test.ts`
- `src/worker/index.ts`
- `src/worker/test/helpers.ts`

**Done when:**

- the checks of the criteria listed above exist as tests, are executable and pass
- `make test` passes
- `make lint` passes

### 3. Queue a link for indexing whenever its indexed text changes (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1

- 3.2 Write queueIndexing(env, userId, linkIds) in src/worker/meaning/indexing.ts: one message {user_id, link_id} for each given link of the user whose text version is past the version of its passages (or that has none), sent in batches of at most 100 with sendBatch, recording when each was queued
- 3.3 Call it for the link after the fetch consumer has stored a fetch result (src/worker/fetcher/queue.ts), after storeEnrichment (src/worker/enrich/queue.ts), and after PATCH /api/v1/links/{id} (src/worker/links/routes.ts)
- 3.4 Call it after a topic or tag is renamed, with every link that carries it, and after a merge, with every link the merge moved onto the survivor (src/worker/search/routes.ts, with those links read through src/worker/search/vocabulary.ts)
- 3.5 A failed send is logged and never fails the write that triggered it; the link stays stale and the backfill picks it up

- 5.3 Refuse in this order, embedding nothing: parseQuery's query_too_long and invalid_filter with field 'q'; no free word as invalid_question with field 'q' and the message 'ask with at least one word'; a limit that is not an integer from 1 to 20 as invalid_limit with field 'limit' and the message 'limit must be an integer from 1 to 20'; an absent limit is 8
- 5.4 Write findPassages(env, userId, words, filters, limit) in the same module, for the later packages to reuse: embed the free words joined by single spaces, query the 100 nearest vectors in the namespace userId, keep the matches scoring at least the threshold, look their ids up among link_passages joined with the user's links under filterConditions (so another user's id or a deleted link's id finds nothing), order by score descending, then link id and position, keep at most 3 per link and cut to limit
